Author’s note:

ITA actually changed its name to IHTA a few years ago, but out of nostalgia I still like to call it ITA. The first time I went there, the institute was still in its old premises in a residential building in the old part of town, and it took me ages to find. In those days, almost every time I looked up from my desk and out of the window, I could see the guy across the way smoking on his balcony.

Five years ago (time flies!) I wrote an article called Into acoustics: a tour of Europe’s best-known acoustics labs. Afterward, quite a few students told me that the article was how they first heard of one institute or another, and that it set them on the road to studying abroad. I am delighted, and honored, that something I wrote could help a little in shaping someone else’s path.

Think of this series as a companion to Giants of acoustics: a look at some of the world’s most impressive acoustics and audio research institutions.

The “old institute” in Burtscheid, in the old part of the city

Singing my heart out at the Christmas party one year

The Institute for Hearing Technology and Acoustics (IHTA) at RWTH Aachen University, formerly the Institute of Technical Acoustics (ITA), is a research institution of worldwide renown specializing in acoustics, hearing technology and psychoacoustics. With its long history, outstanding research and wealth of project results, IHTA has become a leader in advancing hearing science and acoustic technology.

History

The Super C building

IHTA was founded in 1963 as the Institute of Technical Acoustics (ITA), with research centered on room acoustics, psychoacoustics, noise control and ultrasonics. In 2021 it was renamed the Institute for Hearing Technology and Acoustics (IHTA) to reflect the growth of its interdisciplinary research in hearing technology and medical acoustics.

Professors and leadership

Current professors

  • Prof. Dr.-Ing. Janina Fels: Director since 2020, working on auditory cognition in virtual environments, binaural technology and psychoacoustics. She leads a number of major projects, such as the German Research Foundation (DFG) Priority Program SPP 2236, “Auditory Cognition in Interactive Virtual Environments” (AUDICTIVE).

  • Prof. Dr.-Ing. Michael Vorländer: Director of ITA from 1996 to 2020 and a world authority on room acoustics and virtual acoustics. Read more in Giants of acoustics, part 1: Michael Vorländer.

Former professors

  • Prof. Wilhelm Janovsky (1963–1971): The founding director of ITA, who specialized in psychoacoustics and vibration analysis.

  • Prof. Heinrich Kuttruff (1972–1995): A pioneer of room acoustics and ultrasonics research, whose book Room Acoustics is the field’s foundational textbook. (The next article in the series will profile Professor Kuttruff in detail.)

Research areas

An acoustics research laboratory

  1. Audiovisual interaction: how multisensory integration can be used in augmented reality.

  2. Binaural technology: advancing 3D audio systems and individualized head-related transfer functions (HRTFs).

  3. Hearing technology: developing devices such as hearing aids, cochlear implants and acoustic couplers.

  4. Noise research: the effects of noise on people and strategies for mitigating them.

  5. Virtual acoustics: simulating real-world sound environments for testing and analysis.

Current projects

The AUDICTIVE project

  1. SPP 2236 AUDICTIVE: auditory cognition in interactive virtual environments.

  2. IEA HPT Annex 63: the psychoacoustic effects of heat pumps.

  3. LowNoise: noise emissions from air-to-water heat pumps, with the aim of making them more compatible with urban environments.

Completed projects

  1. Real-time auralization of aircraft noise: developed real-time methods for simulating sound propagation along curved paths.

  2. Room auralization: improved algorithms for high-accuracy room acoustics simulation.

Notable alumni

IHTA graduates have gone on to considerable success around the world, for example:

  • Klaus Genuit: founder of HEAD acoustics GmbH, a global leader in sound quality analysis tools.

  • Hans-Wilhelm Gierlich: has made important contributions to telecommunications acoustics.

Books by the institute’s professors

  1. Room Acoustics and Acoustics by Heinrich Kuttruff: key textbooks used widely in academia.

  2. Auralization by Michael Vorländer: a comprehensive introduction to sound simulation methods for virtual reality applications.

  3. Chapters written by IHTA professors in the Springer Handbook of Acoustics, covering psychoacoustics and room acoustics.
